subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` reject every existing ownerless session row, matching the shipped `sessions.delete` fail-closed rule?
rationale: The code can enforce either policy, but accepting loss of plugin patch authority for legacy ownerless rows is a security and upgrade boundary that requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patch calls unless the transaction-selected row has the same explicit `pluginOwnerId`, while operators and non-plugin clients retain management access.

options.title: Add an explicit migration policy
options.body: Define and prove a trusted doctor or owner-specific migration before enforcing the patch fence on legacy ownerless rows.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patch calls unless the transaction-selected row has the same explicit `pluginOwnerId`, while operators and non-plugin clients retain management access.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS identifies this team for Gateway security-sensitive ownership, and the decision concerns cross-plugin authorization.
